text:
sara: FYI rack58 is throwing repeated NVLink flaps + Xid 31 bursts since 03:20 UTC. ECC counters trending up on cards 1/3/5. Not a thermal ramp — temps stable around 42C.

miguel: saw the spike on the dashboard. correlates with the generator transfer last night? there were floor maintenance crews near pod C.

kai: confirmed — infra telemetry shows short-duration vibration events from the datacenter accelerometer cluster at 03:15-03:25 UTC. amplitude ~0.9g peak, localized to rack row C7.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260087 — "Intermittent NVLink/ECC spikes — rack58". Pager duty notified.

sara: stack trace from the driver on one of the affected nodes — posting snippet:
```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00.0): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus.
kernel: nvidia: GPU 0: link down - NVLINK error, retrying
perfmon: ecc_corrected_errors[GPU0]=124 -> 278 over 30m
```

miguel: those "fall off the bus" messages + sub-10ms NVLink flaps are classic mechanical coupling to connectors. We should treat this as a vibration-induced microfracture candidate, not a firmware regression.

hardware-team: Agree. On past events we saw solder microfractures or loose NVLink retainers after heavy floor jacks. We did scheduled UPS transfer at 03:12 and a forklift passed at 03:05 nearby in the logs.

nate: Action plan suggestion: 1) cordon + drain affected nodes 2) migrate running Dedicated slots to eu-west-1 temporarily 3) run accelerated NVLink link diagnostics and serial-match adjacent card errors 4) prepare RMAs for cards with rising ECC.

sara: doing cordon/drain now. command: `kubectl drain gpu-r58-n[01-04] --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

kai: I've bumped autoscaler to prevent new GPU pods scheduling on racks C6-C8 until 18:00 UTC. Also added a node taint `vibration/suspect=true:NoSchedule`.

ops-bot: Evacuation complete: 4 nodes drained (gpu-r58-n01..n04). Jobs relocated.

miguel: ran nvlink diag on one drained node — `nvidia-smi nvlink -s` shows intermittent link down events with low BER but reproducible under small mechanical taps.

hardware-team: we pulled the PCIe/NVLink bridges and reseated two cards. Visual inspection found hairline fracture on retainer clip and tiny solder seam crack near NVLink pad on GPU serial GPC-3491. Taking high-res photos and logging to hw-ticket-4872.

sara: sample of serials with ECC delta >100 in 6h: [GPC-3491, GPC-3493, GPC-3497, GPC-3500] — those are all same manufacturing week batch (lot-2025W43).

miguel: cross-referencing lot numbers with vendor — provisioning team: recommend we quarantine the rest of lot-2025W43 in the pool and treat as possible bad batch.

hardware-team: agreed. we'll RMA the 4 flagged cards and pre-emptively inspect remaining 12 cards of the lot in cold-swap window. Requesting spare pool allocation 4xA100 + 2xA40 for swap.

nate: what's the ETA on hardware swap? need to update customers on Dedicated latency SLOs.

hardware-team: scheduling on-site window tomorrow 09:00-12:00 PT. RMA tickets created with partner.

miguel: short-term mitigation for production — enable prefix/KV cache boost to reduce NVLink pressure and throttle long-context batch jobs to 60% concurrency. That should lower inter-GPU link utilization.

sara: implemented concurrency throttle and adjusted batching in routing policy. Observed Xid frequency drop ~70% after drain + throttle.

kai: posting root-cause hypothesis for the postmortem draft: mechanical vibration during generator transfer + possible manufacturing microfracture in lot-2025W43 -> intermittent NVLink contact loss -> ECC bursts and Xid 31 -> job failures and degraded throughput.

miguel: proposed follow-ups:
- quarantine lot-2025W43 and do full inspection/laser imaging
- vendor quality escalation + request manufacturing traceability for solder reflow profile
- datacenter ops: stricter exclusion zone during heavy machinery ops near GPU rows, add vibration dampers under racks C6-C8
- infra: add automated accelerometer-based trigger to preemptively drain nodes if vibration >0.5g for 5s

hardware-team: will add photos + serial logs to hw-ticket-4872 and ship RMAs. Also will test a rubber isolation pad prototype on one rack tomorrow.

nate: cost note — RMA + spare usage and planned inspection = ~ $48k one-off + ~2% capacity hit for 24-36h. I'll file cost impact to infra-budget.

sara: tagging follow-ups into postmortem doc. interim status: mitigations in place, RMAs queued, quarantine active. Will keep updates here. :white_check_mark:

kai: thanks all. once hardware confirms replacement results we can close INC-20260087 and publish RCA to eng-infra/postmortems.

miguel: +1. also adding an alert rule to correlate accelerometer spikes with GPU Xid rate so we get earlier detection.

ops-bot: INC-20260087 updated: status -> mitigation, next update 2026-01-13 15:00 UTC.

hardware-team: quick note — initial RMA batch approved. replacement ETA 48h.

sara: closing loop for today, will post postmortem draft link when ready. thanks everyone. :v:
